question.leadin: Name these pieces of legislation aimed at the British colonies.
question.text: This collection of punitive measures, also known as the Coercive Acts, included the Quartering Act, and forbade un-approved gatherings of more than five people.
question.clue: Following the passage of these laws, Thomas Hutchinson was replaced byThomas Gage as one colony's governor.

swap.leadin: This man was one of the leaders of the capture of Fort Ticonderoga, and he married Peggy Shippen, a Loyalist and close friend of British military leader John Andre.
swap.text: Name this Revolutionary War traitor who intended to surrender West Point to the British in exchange for 20,000 pounds.
swap.clue: This man successfully defended Bemis Heights during the Battle of Saratoga, but felt he did not get enough credit for it.

question.leadin: Give the following about important signatures in American history.
question.text: The large, elaborate signature of this President of the Continental only appears on the "engrossed" copy of the Declaration of Independence that was signed in August, 1776.
question.clue: This first governor of an independent Massachusetts was closely aligned with Samuel Adams, and neither of them were pardoned by Thomas Gage following the Boston Tea Party.

swap.leadin: This legislation applied not only to practical paper items, but also to playing cards.
swap.text: Name this 1765 Act of Parliament that taxed paper items in the American colonies. It irked Americans who did not wish to be taxed without representation.
swap.clue: A Congress named for this act held in New York passed the "Declaration of Rights and Grievances" which in part called for the end of taxation without representation.

question.text: This founding father created the "Join, or Die" image. He also invented the bifocals and ascertained the electric nature of lightning by flying a kite in a storm.
question.clue: One of this man's political illustrations depicts a snake segmented into eight pieces.

swap.leadin: This general's namesake administrative code gave British people higher status in India than native inhabitants.
swap.text: Name this Governor-General of India, who had earlier surrendered to George Washington at Yorktown.
swap.clue: In another war, he served under General William Howe during the campaigns for New York City and Philadelphia, and he later defeated the army of Horatio Gates at the Battle of Camden.

question.text: This general of the Continental Army led a miscalculated assault against the British during the battle, the failure of which led to him being court-martialed.
question.clue: This man wrote numerous letters to Congress during the New York campaign, seeking to replace his superior, George Washington.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Espionage Front during the American Revolution.
swap.text: This American spy who was hanged in New York after stating "I only regret, that I have but one life to lose for my country"
swap.clue: Robert Rogers recognized this man in a tavern, where he was apprehended by the Queen's Rangers and hung shortly afterwards.

question.text: This loser at Saratoga was known as "Gentleman Johnny" and took Fort Ticonderoga and Fort Edward before losing at Saratoga.
question.clue: This British general commanded at Saratoga. He was to rejoin William Howe in Albany following the battle, but was abandoned by Howe and had to surrender outright.

swap.leadin: This commander's infantry were slaughtered by a British ambush in the Little Egg Harbor Massacre.
swap.text: Name this Polish count who died at the Battle of Savannah. In 2019, researchers announced that this "Father of the American Cavalry" was most likely intersex.
swap.clue: With Michael Kovats, this Eastern European nobleman reformed the American cavalry during the Revolutionary War.

question.leadin: This person likely had the real name Mary Hayes, but may have simply been an amalgamation of a number of different women.
question.text: Name this woman who got her nickname from repeatedly carrying water in the Continental Army's camp. During the Battle of Monmouth, this woman allegedly stepped in for her wounded husband on a cannon crew.
question.clue: This woman fought at the Battle of Monmouth during the Revolutionary War. According to legend, her husband William collapsed during the battle, and she took his place manning artillery.

swap.text: The tea-dumpers were drawn from this secret organization, led in part by Samuel Adams. They were responsible for the tarring and feathering of many a British tax collector.
swap.answerHtml: the Sons of Liberty [accept Sons of Violence or Sons of Iniquity from any turncoats out there]
swap.clue: Members of this group were responsible for the death of William Dudingston and aided Abraham Whipple in the capture of a ship in Narragansett Bay.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Russian navy.
question.text: This American naval officer joined Catherine the Great's navy for a short-lived campaign on the Black Sea.
question.clue: He obtained a reputation for cruelty after flogging the carpenter Mungo Maxwell and running-through the leader of a mutiny, causing him to change his name after fleeing Tobago in 1773.

swap.leadin: The plan was to force the British army marching from Kennett Square into a fight at Chadds Ford.
swap.text: Name this September, 1777 battle of the American Revolution which saw Howe defeat Washington and the British take Philadelphia, named after the creek it occurred on.
swap.clue: General von Knyphausen led the flanking attack that ended this battle, which was followed by a defeat for Anthony Wayne known as the Paoli Massacre.

question.text: Stephen Van Rensselaer married a woman from this family, the daughter of a Revolutionary War general who planned the Saratoga Campaign before he was replaced by Horatio Gates. A woman born to this family discovered the Reynolds Pamphlet while pregnant.
question.answerHtml: Schuyler family [or the Schuylers; accept Peggy Schuyler or Elizabeth Schuyler]

swap.text: This American lieutenant colonel at Cowpens was legendarily saved from death by an unnamed Black soldier, who shot a charging British cornet. He was the cousin of a later President.

question.leadin: This man lost the Battle of Oriskany after being ambushed by a force under Nicholas Herkimer, after which this man was forced to give up the siege of Fort Stanwix.
question.text: Identify this Lieutenant Colonel who was thus unable to meet up with his superior as planned during the Saratoga campaign.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about some forts in early American history.
swap.text: This fort was the site of two treaties signed with the Iroquois. The second treaty named for this fort was signed in 1784 and saw the Iroquois surrender a vast amount of territory in Western Pennsylvania.
swap.clue: On his mother's side, Melville descended from Peter Gansevoort, who led the American defense of this location. The Battle of Oriskany preceded the unsuccessful British siege on this location, which caused Barry St. Leger to be unable to reinforce General Burgoyne at Saratoga.

question.leadin: Name these Revolutionary War battles, FTPE.
question.text: This 1781 engagement in modern-day Greensboro, North Carolina, was a victory for the British under Cornwallis over a force led by Nathaniel Greene. When Charles James Fox heard that the British lost a fourth of their men, he announced that "Another such victory would end the British army!"
question.clue: Shortly before this battle, Henry Lee defeated Dr. John Pyle's forces in "Pyle's Massacre" by posing as Banastre Tarleton, an incident that hurt British morale during it.

swap.text: Ellsworth succeeded this South Carolina native as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court after this man became the only appointee to that position not to be confirmed.
swap.clue: This first Governor of South Carolina after the colonial period, who also served as President of South Carolina.
